key_insight: TRCGL-Net improves rare disease chest X-ray classification by combining synthetic tail-class data generation, attention-based feature refinement, and label co-occurrence modeling.
clinical_relevance: This could help AI systems detect uncommon chest X-ray findings more reliably in imbalanced real-world datasets.
method: Text-guided conditional diffusion generates realistic tail-class X-ray samples.
Channel reweighting and class-aware attention sharpen disease-relevant features and lesion regions.
A graph convolution model captures label co-occurrence across diagnoses.
evidence_signal: On PadChest, the method reported tail-class mAP 0.4904, overall mAP 0.4408, and mAUC 0.8989, outperforming state-of-the-art methods in the abstract.
watch_item: Synthetic image quality and label-co-occurrence learning may not generalize equally well across hospitals, scanners, or disease distributions.
paper_title: TRCGL-Net: A Long-Tailed Multi-Label Chest X-Ray Classification Framework with Generative Data Augmentation and Label Co-Occurrence Modeling
